Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone, then one. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 FY2024 results. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Innovation Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will touch on key elements of our performance, including gross margin guidance and the assumptions behind it, results across our core categories and brands, the competitive landscape and our responses, geographic splits between developed and emerging markets, market share trends by category and region, our capital expenditure plans, and the pricing actions we've taken along with their sales impact. We'll also cover supply chain progress, marketing initiatives, sustainability efforts, digital advancements, and our outlook.

I will now turn the call over to Maria Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Maria Chen:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $3.4 billion, representing a 4.8% increase compared to the prior year, with organic growth of 5.2%. Gross margin was 52.3%, up 50 basis points year-over-year and 20 basis points sequentially, driven by pricing discipline, supply chain productivity gains, and favorable mix shifts. Operating income was $685 million, up 6.2%, and diluted earnings per share were $1.32. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me dive deeper into our performance across key categories and brands, where we saw resilient growth in a challenging macroeconomic backdrop. Our CPG portfolio spans four core pillars: Beauty & Personal Care, Household Care, Nutrition & Wellness, and Grooming Essentials. Organic net sales grew 5.2%, with volumes up 1.8%, mix up 1.5% from premiumization, and pricing at 1.9%. This beat broader CPG averages, which showed flat-to-down volumes per NielsenIQ and IRI amid inflation-driven downtrading.

Beauty & Personal Care, 38% of sales, grew 7.1% organically, doubling the U.S. beauty market's 3.2% per NPD. VitaGlow skincare shone with 12% growth from the Clean Radiance launch using 95% natural actives and recyclable packaging, gaining 2.2 share points to 14.5% in facial skincare per Kantar. Our AI skin diagnostic app now serves 15 million e-commerce users, boosting premium mix by 4 points. North America led at 9%, EMEA softened 2% on inflation, and APAC surged 11% via Tmall and JD.com.

Household Care, 25% of sales, rose 4.3% against a 1.1% category contraction. PureClean laundry grew 8% with PowerPods cutting plastic 30% and lifting U.S. penetration 1.5 points to 28% per IRI. We gained 1.1 share points, especially in Europe with EcoShield cleaners up 15% on bio-enzymes and Green Deal support. LatAm added 6% via value packs.

Nutrition & Wellness, 22% of sales, accelerated 6.8%, beating the 4.5% functional foods market. NutriVive bars and shakes grew 14% with 20g plant-based protein, aligning with vegan trends. DTC subscriptions hit 18% mix, share rose to 11.2% in health bars. APAC boomed 13%, EMEA 5%, North America 4%.

Grooming Essentials, 15% of sales, grew 3.9% in a flat market. FreshEdge razors advanced 9% via subscription model with 2.5 million users and bamboo handles, gaining 0.7 points to 16.8% U.S. share.

This reflects our Elevate & Optimize framework: divesting low-growth items like canned soups for $250 million, investing $450 million in R&D for microbiome and circular packaging targeting 50% recycled content by 2027. E-commerce at 22% yields 15% higher margins, S&OP AI cut stockouts to 2%. North America grew 4.8%, EMEA 3.1%, APAC 8.2%, LatAm 5.5%. We expect Q4 category growth of 4-6% with innovation and share gains.

Turning to geographic performance, developed markets were 58% of our $3.4 billion sales at $2.0 billion, up 1% reported but flat organically, with volumes down 2% offset by 2% pricing. North America, 32% of group, grew 2% on Health & Wellness like Always Fresh yogurts and Ariel EcoWash gaining 1.2 share points. Europe was flat on sentiment weakness, countered by AI planograms boosting distribution 8%. Japan up 3% on snacking.

Emerging markets, 42% at $1.4 billion, grew 14% reported, 12% organically, volumes +7%, pricing 5%. APAC ex-Japan led 18% on Surf Excel sachets gaining 2.5 points in India. China rebounded 15% via Olay on Douyin. LatAm 16% on Oral-B bundles. MEA 10% with localized Dove.

Developed sees shrinkflation fatigue, so GCB Rewards app with 50 million users lifts baskets 5%. Emerging urbanization adds 150 million consumers; micro-dosing boosts trial 30%. $250 million localization cuts COGS 8%. We guide developed 1-3%, emerging 10-13% for FY24 organic.

On market share trends, we gained 80 basis points overall to 24.2%, 11th straight quarter. Beverages, 42% sales, up 150 bps to 31.8% NA sports drinks on FreshBurst, 220 bps APAC to 18.7%. Snacks, 28%, +90 bps NA to 26.5% on NutriCrunch, +180 bps LatAm. Beauty/personal care +110 bps to 23.1%, 280 bps APAC. Home care +60 bps to 22.8%, 250 bps LatAm.

Our Win with Precision includes SKU pruning, digital shelf at <2% OOS, 100% recyclable beverages lifting equity 7 points. Q4 gains of 70-100 bps via e-com and GenAI trade optimizer.

Now, pricing actions: Q3 sales pyramid showed +6.8% price/mix offsetting -2.6% volume. Average list hikes 4.5%, via AI elasticity modeling. Snacks +5.2% list, NRR +4.7%, sales +5.6%. Beverages +6.1%, +8.4% sales. Household/personal +3.8%. NA +5.1%, Europe +4.2%, emerging +9.2%. Elasticity -1.4x beat peers; 220 bps margin expansion. Q4 3-5% pricing for +5-6% sales contribution.

Competitive activity was intense, category dollars +2.1% vs. 3.2% CPI. NA CPG share flat at 14.2%. Fabric care: P&G Tide up A&P 15%, we optimized trade for 2.2x ROI, AI pricing defended 92% volume. Beverages: Coke/Pepsi stole share, we launched Zero Compromise $120M campaign, gained 3.2 points Amazon. Snacks: Mondelez/Kellogg's pressured, Baked Protein Crisps won 1.8 points ACV. APAC AR filters gained 12% China. Fortress Share reallocates $300M to digital, blockchain differentiates.

Capex guidance $2.8 billion, 4.2% sales, up 8%. Manufacturing/supply chain 45% $1.26B: AI maintenance cuts downtime 25%, NA capacity $630M, EMEA green retrofits. Sustainability 25% $700M: rPET lines, Scope 3 blockchain. Digital 20% $560M: micro-ful DCs, AI sensing. R&D 10% $280M health platforms. 10-15% contingency, 2.5-year payback, $0.75 EPS FY25.

Finally, gross margin outlook: Q4 and FY2025 at 52.5-53.0%, +50-80 bps from FY2024's 52.0%, best since FY2021. Pillars: pricing/mix +120-150 bps (2-3% NA, 3.5% EMEA, 5% LatAm); supply chain +150-200 bps ($450M YTD savings, ZBP AI yields, hedged cocoa $4200/ton, DC consolidation); inputs -100-150 bps (3-4% inflation, cocoa flat+5%); FX -40-60 bps. Regional: NA 53.0-53.5%, EMEA 52.0-52.5%, APAC 51.5-52.0%, LatAm 53.5-54.0%. Structural to 55%+ FY2027 via reshaping, digital $150M CapEx, 60% recyclable.

Following my remarks, David will update on marketing and brands.

David Patel:
Thank you, Maria. We continue to see strong performance across key brands. Marketing investments drove consumer engagement, especially our Zero Compromise campaign blending TV and TikTok for 7% trial lift. Shopper marketing in Revive drinks yielded 2x ROI, e-com exclusives boosted premium mix, and personalization via apps enhanced loyalty. YouGov scores up 5 points portfolio-wide.

After me, Lisa will discuss supply chain.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, David. Our focus on optimization enhanced efficiency and resilience. Advanced analytics improved forecasting and inventory, ZBP Phase III cut waste via AI yields—like 18% downtime at Ohio plant. Supplier portal locked cocoa hedges, logistics consolidation dropped freight 12%, regenerative soy for 40% sourcing with carbon credits. Localization mitigated FX, stockouts to 2%.

Finally, Tom will share innovation insights.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Lisa. We're excited about our pipeline. New PureClean PowerPods show promising early results, with 15% trial and share gains in laundry on concentrated format and ocean-safe design. VitaGlow Clean Radiance and NutriCore plant-based bars up 15% penetration, microbiome formulations and functional beverages position us for growth. $450M R&D targets circular packaging and alt-proteins.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions as before. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan.

John Smith:
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce packaging waste and the associated cost savings?

Lisa Wong:
Thanks, John. Packaging waste reduction is core to our sustainability pillar, with $700 million CapEx including $120 million for rPET conversion in Mexico targeting 50% recycled content by 2027. PowerPods cut plastic 30%, EcoShield uses recyclable formats, and we've hit 60% recyclable portfolio-wide. This yielded $50 million savings YTD via circular projects, plus 2-3% EU premiums under Green Deal. Blockchain tracks 20% chain for provenance, monetizing credits—expect $100 million cumulative by FY26.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Davis with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Davis:
How are you leveraging data analytics to personalize your marketing efforts and improve customer engagement?

David Patel:
Great question, Emily. Our AI-driven personalization is transforming engagement—VitaGlow app with 15 million users tailors regimens, boosting repeat 25%. GCB Rewards 50 million members get personalized coupons via Kroger data for 1.5x repeats. TikTok AR filters and WeChat Mini Programs drove 12% China share, bundling lifts baskets 14-28%. GenAI optimizes trade promos at 3:1 ROI, e-com at 22% sales with 15% higher margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with Barclays.

Mike Johnson:
What is the expected impact of recent commodity price increases on your gross margins?

Maria Chen:
Mike, commodities are a wildcard, but we've hedged proactively. Assume 3-4% input inflation FY2025, down from 5.5%. Cocoa flat to +5% hedged half, palm/sunflower +4% moderated, PET +2%, paper +3%. Labor 4% capped by automation, Europe energy -15%. Overall -100-150 bps drag offset by productivity. LatAm high pricing cushions; if cocoa >$5500, +200 bps hit, but elasticity -0.3x gives runway. FY2025 52.5-53.0% holds.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Laura Chen:
Can you discuss the competitive landscape and any emerging trends that are impacting your market share?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Laura. Competition is fierce—P&G up A&P 15% on Tide, private labels at 22% laundry—but we held 98% core share, grew EPS 7%. Responses like Zero Compromise regained 3.2 Amazon points, AI pricing defended volume, Baked Crisps won ACV vs. Mondelez. Trends: premiumization, e-com 22%, sustainability—our 65% rPET leads Unilever. Emerging: urbanization in APAC/LatAm, health functionals. Fortress Share and war room dashboard keep us ahead; 80 bps overall gain to 24.2%.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your thoughtful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders—structural margins to 55%+, balanced growth, innovation velocity. We look forward to updating you next quarter.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
